claims.statement: The /mcp endpoint accepts three bearer credential kinds: OAuth access tokens from the PKCE authorization-code flow, OAuth access tokens from RFC 8628 device authorization, and scoped API keys (strap_key_ new, creed_key_ legacy), resolved by resolveMcpCredential in app/mcp/route.ts.

Every modern credential binds exactly one Personal or Company Strap plus a maximum access mode (read-only, proposal-only, or direct); applyCredentialMode clamps each section's agentPermission to the lower of section policy and the credential ceiling before dispatch, blanking writeToken for read-only and directEditToken for non-direct modes.

If an explicit grant becomes inaccessible, resolveMcpState returns an empty write-less state rather than widening to the owner's Personal Strap; only OAuth tokens positively identified as pre-explicit-grant (creed_grants_explicit false with no grants) may use the legacy personal fallback via allowLegacyPersonalFallback, and API keys never use it.

For a Company Strap target, each section's effective agent permission is the lower of the Company member/section ceiling (creed_member_section_permissions, direct for owner/admin) and the member's own agent permission; hidden sections are dropped, and a revoked membership returns the empty state instead of falling through to the Personal loader.

The authorization-code flow is a minimal OAuth 2.1 server with opaque tokens, mandatory PKCE S256 verified in constant time, single-use 60-second codes claimed atomically by flipping used_at, public clients with no secret, and loopback redirect port tolerance per RFC 8252.

issueTokenPair issues a 1-hour access token and a 30-day rotating refresh token, storing SHA-256 hashes for lookup plus AES-256-GCM ciphertext via lib/secret-crypto.ts keyed by STRAP_ENCRYPTION_SECRET (or legacy CREED_ENCRYPTION_SECRET), and persists per-Strap grants to oauth_token_creeds best-effort so a failed grant only narrows access.

Refresh rotation is single-use: rotateRefreshToken carries the old token's per-Strap grants onto the rotated token and claims the row in Postgres by revoking a still-live one, so concurrent refreshes and replayed refresh tokens cannot both issue replacement pairs.

/revoke implements RFC 7009: the caller must prove the owning client_id so one client cannot revoke another's grant, both access and refresh token forms are accepted, and an unknown token still returns success so the endpoint cannot be used as a token oracle; CLI client roster rows are also deleted on revoke.

Browser consent uses a Better Auth session resolved via lib/request-auth.ts and lib/auth/server.ts (BETTER_AUTH_SECRET), not a Supabase session; /authorize and /authorize/decision re-resolve the user from the session, never a form field.

The consent screen exposes no mode picker: it records a direct ceiling and relies on live per-section policy to narrow actual rights, and a solo Personal user gets no Strap picker while a user in Company Straps gets a picker scoped to exactly one Strap.

RFC 8414 authorization-server metadata advertises /authorize, /device/authorize, /token, /revoke, /register, the authorization_code/refresh_token/device_code grants, S256-only PKCE, none token auth, and scopes read/propose/direct_edit; RFC 9728 protected-resource metadata points at /mcp and is also served at the path-inserted /.well-known/oauth-protected-resource/mcp.

RFC 7591 dynamic registration at /register issues strap_client_ ids with no secret and allows custom app schemes per RFC 8252, blocking only javascript/data/vbscript/file schemes; up to ten redirect_uris are accepted, so consent and exact redirect matching matter more than the displayed client name.

RFC 8628 device authorization issues a strap_dc_ device code stored as a SHA-256 digest, an eight-character user code from a 32-symbol unambiguous alphabet, the /device verification URI, a 10-minute lifetime, and an initial 5-second poll interval.

Device grant modes are capped by the requested OAuth scope via deviceGrantModesForScope: read yields read-only, propose yields up to proposal-only, direct_edit yields up to direct, and capDeviceGrantMode caps the user-chosen mode to that ceiling.

Device polling is serialized in Postgres by the consume_oauth_device_authorization SQL function, which locks the row and returns authorization_pending, slow_down (incrementing interval by 5 up to 300), approved (one-time consumption to consumed), access_denied, expired_token, or invalid_grant (client mismatch); durable timing lives in Postgres while lib/rate-limit.ts only gates endpoint abuse.

Device user-code verification via record_oauth_device_verification locks the pending row and auto-denies after 10 attempts; /device/decision re-derives approval, validates the chosen Strap belongs to the user, caps the mode, and audit-logs approve/deny.

One-time-visible API keys are created by createHeadlessKey from 32 random bytes with strap_key_ prefix; only the SHA-256 digest and a short display prefix persist, the plaintext is returned once, expiry is bounded to 366 days, and resolution checks revocation, expiry, and creator membership and records last_used_at best-effort.

Headless-access APIs under app/api/app/headless-access/** require a Better Auth session (requireApiAuth) and let any current Strap member list, create (with explicit mode and optional expiry), or revoke keys for that Strap; the legacy ?token= query-string fallback was removed from the read API so tokens stay out of URLs.

MCP supports JSON-RPC tools/resources/prompts, request batching of 1 to 64 objects with a 12 MB body cap, CORS discovery, and protocol 2025-06-18 returned by initialize along with MCP_INSTRUCTIONS; GET returns 405 because Strap pushes no SSE stream.

MCP discovery is Strap-first: tools/list advertises canonical strap_-prefixed names produced by replacing creed_/Creed/creed in the internal definitions, and the 401 WWW-Authenticate header advertises scope read propose direct_edit and the protected-resource metadata URL.

The MCP compatibility surface must not be renamed: LEGACY_TOOL_NAMES maps canonical strap_ names back to creed_ aliases and the dispatcher accepts both, keeping list_creeds, read_creed, propose_creed_update, direct_edit_creed, creed_update_section, creed_create_section, creed_delete_section, creed_rename_section, creed_recolor_section, creed_append_to_section, creed_reorder_section, creed_get_section, creed_search, creed_get_recent_activity, creed_get_quality_report, the creed://profile resource, and unprefixed get_write_policy/list_sections callable.

Conditional tool exposure aligns discovery with the credential ceiling: read-only credentials receive only read tools (mutation names filtered out), and write-capable credentials still hide the legacy direct_edit_strap alias when no section allows direct edits.

MCP skills (strap_list_skills, strap_get_skill, strap_export_skill, strap_publish_skill) are backed by the retained strap_skills_read and strap_skill_publish SQL procedures; skill reads/exports/publications must be individual requests, publishing requires direct access plus owner/admin role and is rate-limited per user, and skill guidance cannot override higher-priority instructions or authorize secret access.

/api/strap, /api/strap/proposals, and /api/strap/write are the canonical direct HTTP paths while /api/creed/** is only a compatibility shim re-exporting the same handler behavior, authentication, and rate limits; lib/creed-data.ts is a deprecated re-export shim of lib/strap-data.ts.

The primary CLI @bvdm/strap (packages/strap) publishes the strap executable for Node 20+, defaults to https://strap.bvdm.ai/mcp, uses browser authorization-code PKCE via the MCP SDK, discovers tools/resources/prompts live, stores credentials per server under STRAP_CONFIG_DIR, and requires HTTPS except explicit localhost loopback; it has no device-flow or API-key login command.

Server precedence for the primary CLI is --server, STRAP_MCP_URL, saved config, then the default URL; logout discovers the revocation endpoint from authorization-server metadata and attempts RFC 7009 refresh-token revocation, removing local credentials regardless.
The legacy creed-cli (packages/creed-cli) exposes creed/creed-cli, defaults to https://creed.md/mcp, is separately configured, and neither CLI reads or migrates the other's credentials.

Rate limiting is process-local in-memory token bucket (lib/rate-limit.ts), suitable for single-region deployments; MCP hashes the bearer value before using it as the rate-limit identifier, and endpoint limits include /register 20/min per IP, /token 60/min per client, /revoke 30/min per IP, /device/authorize 20/min per client, /device/verify 10/min per IP, /mcp 120/min per hashed bearer, and skill publish 20/min per user.
